name: Scrollbar
description: A thin scrollbar with no track that is drawn in the text colour, so it follows every theme. Put it on any scroll container, or on the page.

classes.ayy-scrollbar: Root, on the element that scrolls (or <html> for the page). 8px gutter, 4px thumb, transparent track.
classes.ayy-scrollbar--hover: Thumb is hidden until the pointer or focus is inside the container.

default.looks: A rounded thumb in the text colour at 22%, on a transparent track.

hover.when: The pointer is over the thumb (Chromium and Safari only)
hover.looks: Thumb darkens to 40% text. With --hover, the whole thumb appears while the pointer is inside the container.

pressed.when: The thumb is being dragged (Chromium and Safari only)

focus.when: Focus is inside the container, with the hover variant
focus.looks: The thumb shows, as it does on hover. The scrollbar itself isn't focusable: give the scroll container tabindex="0" so the keyboard can scroll it.

disabled.none: A scrollbar can't be disabled; remove overflow instead.

sizes.width: 8px by default; set --ayy-scrollbar-size on the container for another gutter. The thumb is the gutter minus 4px. Firefox only offers its own thin scrollbar and ignores the size.

props.hover: boolean — show the thumb only while the pointer or focus is inside.

a11y: Scrolling stays native: wheel, touch, keyboard and assistive technology all work. The component only changes how the bar looks.
A scroll container that has no focusable content needs tabindex="0" and a label, or keyboard users can't scroll it. The React component sets tabindex="0".
Forced colours: the thumb is drawn in system colours.
do: Use the scrollbar on scroll containers inside a page: lists, panels, code, menus.
Put it on <html> to thin the page's own scrollbar.
Use the hover variant where the bar would crowd a dense, quiet surface.
dont: Don't use it to hide scrolling — to hide the bar altogether, give the user another way to scroll.
Don't use it as a progress indicator — use Progress, or the reading-progress bar.
Don't make it thicker to match touch targets; touch devices draw their own overlay bars.
